output:
Short answer: consider the Meadowlight Lamp as your primary candidate for an energy-efficient office desk lamp.

Why I recommend Meadowlight (evidence from your saved catalog/memory)
- Your facilities guide lists the Meadowlight Lamp specifically as an “energy-efficient task light for office desks.”
- The catalog describes the Meadowlight as “independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency” and as a “certified low-energy product for focused desk work.”
- Procurement guidance in your handbook explicitly recommends the Meadowlight for sustainable office lighting upgrades.

What in those statements should be verified before purchase
The catalog claims are a good starting point but need concrete technical confirmation. Ask the vendor or check the spec sheet (and independent test reports) for:
- Which certification(s)? (e.g., ENERGY STAR, DLC — the catalog’s phrase “independently certified” should be linked to a specific program or lab report.)
- Power draw (watts) and lumen output (lumens) — to calculate lumens per watt (efficacy).
- Typical on-desk illuminance (lux) or recommended lumens for typical desk distances.
- Color temperature (CCT, in K) and color rendering index (CRI) — important for visual comfort and accurate color work.
- Dimmability/flicker metrics and driver quality (flicker % / modulation if available).
- Rated lifetime (hours) and lumen maintenance (L70, L80).
- Warranty length and warranty terms.
- Material/recyclability and any EPEAT or circularity claims (if sustainability is a priority).
- Price, bulk discounts, lead time, and availability.
- Compatibility with your office controls (dimmers, occupancy sensors, building lighting controls).
- Independent lab test reports or third-party listings (to substantiate “independently certified” and efficiency claims).

Practical selection criteria / minimum targets to request or compare
- LED lamp (yes, Meadowlight appears to be marketed as low-energy — confirm it’s LED).
- Efficacy: look for ≥90 lm/W for good efficiency (higher is better).
- Task illuminance: aim for ~300–500 lux at the work plane for typical office tasks (adjust based on tasks).
- CRI ≥80 (≥90 if color-critical tasks).
- Adjustable head/arm and beam control to reduce glare and light spill.
- Dimmable driver and low flicker if staff are sensitive to flicker.
- Clear warranty (3+ years preferred for office deployments).

Next steps I can take for you
- I can fetch the Meadowlight spec sheet and certification details from your catalog or procurement files (if you want me to look up specific documents).
- If you want a shortlist of other comparable energy-efficient desk lamps, tell me any must-have features (dimmable, USB, wireless charging, motion sensor), budget per lamp, and how many desks you’re outfitting.

Which claims I can try to verify for you now
- Exact certification name and certificate number (if in your catalog files).
- Watts, lumens, lm/W, CCT, CRI, lifetime, and warranty (if spec sheet is available).

Tell me whether you want me to pull the Meadowlight technical datasheet and certification documents from your catalog/memory, or provide criteria and sample alternative models for comparison.
